title: Why a Smell Can Instantly Trigger an Old Memory
hook: Ever smell something and instantly relive an old memory?

narration.text: The scents we encounter can powerfully transport us back in time.
This happens because your sense of smell is wired differently from your other senses.
When you inhale, odour molecules travel directly to your olfactory bulb.
This bulb has direct, immediate connections to the limbic system, the brain's emotional and memory centre.
Other senses, like sight and hearing, process information through different brain areas first.
This unique pathway means smells bypass the usual processing, heading straight for your memories.
It explains why a particular perfume or a baking smell can bring a rush of nostalgia.
What smell instantly brings back a vivid memory for you?

description: Have you ever wondered why a particular smell can immediately take you back to a specific moment or feeling from your past? It is all down to a unique direct link in your brain's architecture. Learn why your sense of smell holds such a powerful key to your personal history.
topic: Why smells can strongly trigger old memories, explaining the direct link between the olfactory bulb and the limbic system.
